content:
Nikhil Sharma: Question for the group: do we want an in-product nudge/banner when we detect “Dedicated is probably better” (sustained throughput, repeated 429s, etc.)? I’m worried it could conflict with AE outreach from the PLG signals pipeline, but also feels like a good self-serve assist.

Ben Carter: +1 on exploring. If we do it, needs strict frequency caps + suppression when sales is already engaged. Otherwise we’ll look spammy.

Stephanie Nguyen: From Sales side: I like it *if* it’s coordinated. Worst case is: banner says “talk to sales” and the AE email hits the same day, plus marketing nurture. That’s 3 touches and we get the SUP-3392-type complaints again.

Markus Klein: Also depends on what the nudge does. If it’s “switch to Dedicated for better throughput,” we should be careful not to promise SLOs we can’t guarantee without scoping. But we can safely say “Dedicated can help with higher concurrency, fewer 429s, predictable capacity.”

Elliot Price: We can measure intent cleanly if the banner links to /docs/dedicated or the Dedicated overview. But please don’t make it a modal with forced click-through; that’ll inflate vanity engagement.

Tyler Benson: Marketing perspective: we should define suppression rules like we did for nurture vs AE outreach. If the banner fires, do we also trigger lifecycle email? Or do we treat the banner as the touch and suppress email for X days?

Nikhil Sharma: Agree. Mechanically, I was thinking: banner only for org admins, only when a “scale/reliability” signal score crosses threshold, and only once per 14 days per workspace.

Ben Carter: Can we align on which signals qualify? I’d propose starting w/ 2 high-confidence cases:
1) Repeated 429s over multiple days + rising token volume
2) Sustained spend velocity above $X/day for Y days (paid accounts)
Team expansion/workspaces is softer and might be a false positive.

Stephanie Nguyen: For #1, that’s great. Those are the ones where the AE outreach feels helpful, not creepy. For spend velocity, we should be careful on trials — “upgrade” prompt to someone using free credits feels off.

Jasmine Liu: CS angle: please don’t show this to existing customers already on Dedicated/Private (obvious), but also watch for accounts that have an assigned CSM (even if still “self-serve”). If there’s an active support escalation, a sales-y banner can land badly.

Markus Klein: +1. Also, if the trigger is “repeated 429s,” we should make sure the banner suggests immediate mitigation steps too (e.g., “check rate limits / contact us for higher limits / consider Dedicated”). Otherwise it reads like “pay us to fix it.”

Elliot Price: Copy suggestion that’s less sales-y:
“Running into rate limits or need higher concurrency? Dedicated capacity can provide predictable throughput. Learn more.”
And add a secondary link: “See best practices” (rate limiting + batching doc).

Tyler Benson: If we include a “best practices” link, we should ensure it doesn’t conflict with the sales CTA. But I like the framing — it’s helpful.

Ben Carter: On suppression: simplest rule is:
- If a HubSpot task was created from a PLG signal in last 7 days for that company, suppress banner
- If banner shown, suppress marketing nurture on Dedicated upgrade theme for 7 days
We can refine later.

Stephanie Nguyen: Re “task created” isn’t the same as “AE contacted.” But it’s a good proxy for pilot. Maybe also suppress if company is in an active sequence / open opp stage.

Ben Carter: If we can read that from HubSpot reliably without adding a bunch of coupling, sure. But for MVP, I’d rather keep it in-product only using our internal signal state + a simple “sales_engaged=true” flag set by the router.

Nikhil Sharma: That’s doable. Router can write back a company property (or internal flag) like `plg_sales_engagement_state` and we can key off it in the app.

Markus Klein: Another nuance: if we show the banner and they click “Learn more,” that should count as intent and probably raise the signal score (or at least add context to the AE). But we should avoid the loop where click -> raises score -> triggers AE -> then banner again.

Elliot Price: Yeah, dedupe key should prevent re-notification. Treat banner clicks as “intent evidence” but not a new signal unless combined with other criteria.

Jasmine Liu: What about accounts that are *already* talking to support about 429s? Can we suppress if there’s an open support ticket? Otherwise they get both “we’re working it” and “upgrade now.”

Nikhil Sharma: Good call. We likely can’t wire support ticket state into the UI for MVP, but we can at least suppress for orgs tagged “support escalation” internally (we have that tag in the console for SRE incident comms). I’ll check w/ Platform.

Tyler Benson: On copy/tone: avoid “you’ve hit X tokens” or “we noticed.” Keep it generic: “If you need…” The privacy optics matter.

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Please no “we detected you’re spending $___.” Also: route the CTA to a lightweight “Talk to us” form that can create a meeting link, but not require it.

Ben Carter: Experiment design: A/B in-product banner vs control for qualifying workspaces. Primary metric: meeting booked within 14 days. Secondary: Dedicated docs views, contact-us submissions. Guardrail: support tickets complaining about outreach.

Nikhil Sharma: Sounds right. Let’s keep it to NA pilot cohort first.

Markus Klein: If we do meetings attribution, we should make sure HubSpot notes capture “banner shown/clicked” so AEs have context.

Ben Carter: Yep. We can log an internal event and the router can append a HubSpot timeline note only if it becomes sales-qualified (don’t want HubSpot noise for every banner view).

Elliot Price: For instrumentation: we should log `banner_eligible`, `banner_shown`, `banner_dismissed`, `banner_cta_clicked`, and the variant. If the CTA goes to docs, add UTM params so we can separate from normal docs traffic.

Nikhil Sharma: Action items:
- Ben: draft MVP eligibility + suppression rules (esp. “sales engaged” flag) and propose thresholds for the 2 high-confidence cases.
- Elliot: propose banner copy + links (Dedicated overview + best practices) and tracking plan.
- Stephanie/Jasmine: sanity-check playbook interaction (when AE outreach should still happen vs not).
- I’ll open a ticket for in-product banner implementation + gating (admin-only, 14d frequency cap) and loop in Platform for the “support escalation” tag feasibility.

Stephanie Nguyen: Works for me. Please share the copy before it goes live; AEs will get questions.

Jasmine Liu: +1 and add a note in the CS handoff doc when banner is enabled so CSMs aren’t surprised.

Ben Carter: Cool. I’ll post a draft in this thread by EOW.

Nikhil Sharma: :thumbsup: let’s do it as an experiment, not a permanent UI change (yet).
